subject: Copywriting
title: Lee Clow: Think Different
description: A fast breakdown of Lee Clow: Think Different for builders.

hook.text: Lee Clow's 1984 Apple commercial aired once during the Super Bowl and never ran again. One showing was enough.

buildup.text: Clow led TBWA\Chiat\Day and became Steve Jobs' creative partner. Together they built Apple's rebellious brand voice.

discovery.text: The 'Think Different' campaign featured Einstein, Lennon, and Gandhi.

twist.text: Apple was nearly bankrupt when 'Think Different' launched.

climax.text: Clow proved that a brand is a story, not a product. His work for Apple is studied in every business school.

punchline.text: One Super Bowl ad, aired once. Changed tech marketing forever.

quiz.question: What was Apple's state when 'Think Different' launched?

details.summary: Lee Clow was the creative genius behind Apple's most iconic advertising, including the 1984 Super Bowl commercial and the 'Think Different' campaign. As chairman of TBWA\Media Arts Lab, he helped Steve Jobs transform Apple from a struggling computer company into the world's most valuable brand.
details.whyItMatters: Clow's work proves that advertising can change a company's trajectory completely. His partnership with Jobs shows how trust between a visionary client and a great creative produces legendary work.
takeaways: He directed Apple's 1984 commercial, often called the greatest TV ad ever
The Think Different campaign helped save Apple from bankruptcy
His decades-long partnership with Jobs produced consistently iconic work

faq.question: What made the Apple 1984 commercial so revolutionary?
faq.answer: Directed by Ridley Scott, it ran only once during the Super Bowl and positioned Apple as a liberator against IBM's conformity. It introduced the Macintosh without showing the product, proving that emotional storytelling could launch a product more powerfully than feature demonstrations.

faq.question: How did Lee Clow and Steve Jobs work together?
faq.answer: Their partnership spanned decades and was built on mutual respect and creative trust. Jobs gave Clow unusual freedom, and Clow gave Jobs brave ideas. When Jobs returned to Apple in 1997, Clow was the first call he made — resulting in Think Different.
